overview:
WARRIORLOG — final architecture. Spine = Design 1 (IndexedDB event log, per-device sole-writer JSONL files on an orphan `data` branch, plan frozen into session.started, closed predicate registry, cache-first shell). Grafts from Design 0: flat ~35-file footprint, legacy Pages publishing from `main` root exactly like the existing SJJ363.github.io site (no Actions deploy, no CI sed stamp), a stale-while-revalidate shell with ETag-diff "update ready" toast instead of a build stamp, program.test.js as a data linter, explicit `load` objects with declared substitution rules, regress-then-hold / rpeCap / 1-step-per-session / time-gated technique steps, CLAUDE.md invariants, and the nav sync dot + Export/Import/Rebuild recovery paths. Fatal-flaw fixes: (1) logs never touch the Pages branch, so two phones committing cannot trigger rebuilds, force laptop rebases, or be destroyed by a code push; (2) commits carry `author:{name:<user>}` so each log commit is attributed to Sean or Cat; (3) events carry `user`, remote paths are `log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl`, reduce() partitions by user, and a pure duo.js derives the co-op/rivalry state — Cat's sets can never fold into Sean's ladders.

Deployment decisions reflected: free org `warriorlog`, repo `warriorlog/warriorlog.github.io`, served from `main` root with `.nojekyll` at https://warriorlog.github.io/ (its own origin, which also removes Design 1's shared-origin token risk). config.js carries `basePath:'/'` as the single deploy value; every asset URL is relative and routing is hash-based, so a sub-path deploy needs at most that one value changed. Local folder `/Users/sjj/Documents/claude projects/warriorlog`, its own git repo, two branches: `main` (app) and `data` (orphan; only the phones write it via the Contents API).

Runtime shape: vanilla HTML/CSS/ES modules, zero dependencies, no bundler. Single source of truth is an append-only event log (session.started, set.logged, session.finished, profile.updated, assessment.recorded, benchmark.recorded, metric.logged, rest.taken, ladder.override…). Ladder positions, XP, level, streak, badges, duo streak, weekly scoreboard and boss-battle progress are NEVER stored; they are recomputed by pure functions reduce() → engine.evalLadders() → gamify() → duo() on every load and after every dispatch. Every set tap awaits an IndexedDB put (<5 ms) before the UI marks it done; sync to GitHub happens later (session finish, app hide, online, 5-min timer, manual), one commit per touched file. Pull happens on app open/resume/after push and reads every other (user,device) partition, which is what powers "partner trained today" and the scoreboard.

Program: 6-day rotation A–F expressed entirely in data/program.json as ladders whose steps carry machine-checkable `advance`/`regress` rules from a closed registry, `requires` strings resolved against the declared equipment, `gate` prerequisites (the 53 lb bell is unlocked by a hinge-ladder position AND a recorded swing-form check), per-user `startFrom` maps fed by the 60-second placement quiz, deload and benchmark schedules. Ladders start low enough for a smaller beginner (wall push-ups, 12 lb goblet, 8 lb press, 20 lb two-hand DB swings) and bridge the 12→20→35→53 gaps with rep ranges, tempo, pauses, 1.5-reps, unilateral variants, density/EMOM and the vest. XP is load-independent so the head-to-head is fair by construction.

Tests: `node --test test/` (Node 24, ESM, no framework) covers reduce, engine (golden plans), gamify, duo, sync (fake fetch), util, events/migrations, and program.test.js lints the data for both users' inventories and placement extremes. Browser verification via `python3 -m http.server` at root and at a sub-path.

All URLs relative, no inline scripts.

Dark theme via CSS custom properties, 56–64 px touch targets, 100dvh + env(safe-area-inset-*), touch-action:manipulation, inputs ≥16 px, prefers-reduced-motion, fixed skeleton sizes (no layout shift). ~300 lines.

PWA manifest: name Warriorlog, short_name Warrior, id ./, start_url ./, scope ./, display standalone, orientation portrait, background/theme #0b0f14, icons 192/512 + maskable 512. Relative so it works at / or /sub/.

Service worker (~90 lines): SHELL list resolved with new URL(p, self.location); cache-first for shell + data JSON; background revalidateShell() with cache:'no-cache' comparing ETags and posting {type:'update-ready'} to clients only after ALL shell files refetched; never intercepts api.github.com or non-GET; CACHE name bumped only when SW logic changes.

What it is, URL, local run, tests, data layout (main vs data branch, per-user paths), PAT creation for each phone, recovery (Rebuild from log / Pull all / Export-Import), token expiry.

Invariants for future sessions: event-sourced (never store totals), single-writer-per-file (log/<user>/<dev>/), logs live ONLY on the data branch, everything relative + hash routes, program changes go in data/*.json + tests, XP must stay load-independent (fairness), never commit tokens, run npm test before push.

Boot + state + hash router + render loop + dispatch(). Loads config/program/exercises/gamification, opens store, migrates + reduces events, registers SW (basePath + 'sw.js'), wires online/visibilitychange/BroadcastChannel/SW messages, wake lock during a session, sync triggers, update toast.
SCHEMA_VERSION, event type constants, makeEvent(type, data, ctx) (id, ts, day, dev, user, v, private), validate(event) → errors[], MIGRATIONS[] + migrateEvent(). Pure.

IndexedDB 'warriorlog' v1 (events / files / meta stores) behind a ~40-line promise wrapper; append(), all(), unsynced(), markSynced(), file sha bookkeeping; localStorage for settings only; in-memory + localStorage snapshot fallback when IDB is unavailable; navigator.storage.persist() on first run.

RULES registry (closed), resolveSteps(ladder, equipment), evalLadder(), isDeloadWeek(), nextWorkout(), prescribe(spec, userState, today) → Plan, fitToTime(), resolveLoad(). Pure, injectable clock.
xpForSession(), levelFor(xp), streak(days), badges(userState, spec) with earnedAt; all constants from data/gamification.json. Pure and load-independent.

Onboarding: who are you (Sean/Cat), equipment (vest weights, dumbbell pairs?, treadmill), 60-second placement quiz → profile.updated + assessment.recorded; token paste is deferred to Settings but linked.

Today: prescription card (workout, est minutes, deload/test-day banner, per-slot targets + why), Start button, partner-trained-today chip, duo streak, pending swing-form-check card, sync dot state, rest-day button.

Session: one exercise card at a time, one-tap DONE per set (pre-filled target reps/load), tap number → bottom sheet (reps/secs/load/RPE steppers), rest timer ring + beep, swipe/next exercise, Finish (session RPE, note), Abandon, Undo toast.
Progress: XP/level bar + rank, streak, ladder map (each ladder's step, next unlock hint, gate status), badges grid, benchmark history as inline SVG.

Duo: partner status (trained today / last session), duo streak, this-week head-to-head scoreboard with 5 relative categories + crowns, last week's result, active boss battle bar (combined vs target), duo badges.
History: sessions by date with prescribed-vs-done, tap to open sets, edit via sheet (emits new set.logged), abandoned/rest days shown.
Body (local-only): weight/waist/etc. entry, trend chart (inline SVG), explicit 'stays on this phone' notice and the syncMetrics opt-in link.

Settings: user identity, GitHub token (masked, Save/Test/Forget, expiry date nag), Sync now + status, Pull all, Rebuild from log, Export/Import JSON, rest timer/sound, install tip, app version (from sw cache ETag), switch user.

The program: phases, templates/rotation, workouts (blocks), ladders (steps with reps/secs/load/requires/gate/advance/regress), placement startFrom maps, deload/regress/rpeCap rules, rest, benchmarks, form checks, load substitution rules.
Exercise library keyed by id: name, muscles, 2–4 cues, stopIf safety note, requires, estSecPerRep, unilateral flag / singleAlt.

XP constants (load-independent), level curve, ranks, streak rules, badge definitions (pred + args), duo config: scoreboard categories, boss battles (metric registry + targets + week windows), duo badges.
Committed PNG icons (iOS needs apple-touch-icon; manifest icons for Android).

Sessions grouping, LWW set edits, done:false deletes, private filtering, per-user partition (Cat's sets never touch Sean's perf), reduce(events) === fold(apply) property, commutativity: same events shuffled/split across files/users derive identical state.

Every RULES predicate pass/fail; advance after N consecutive hits; rpeCap blocks a hit; regress after 2 misses then hold; 1 step/session cap; gate blocks + unlockHint; ladder.override; equipment filtering + singleAlt; deload by week and fatigue; rotation/test-day; time fitting; golden Plans for fixture histories (both users).
XP determinism and load-independence (same reps at different steps → same XP), level thresholds, streak with 1 rest/7 and grace, badges earnedAt.

partnerTrainedToday, duo streak rules, weekly scoreboard fairness fixtures (stronger user with more absolute reps but fewer targets hit loses the category), boss combined progress + defeat, duo badges, ISO week boundaries.

Fake fetch scripts: 201 create, 200 update, 409→GET→merge→PUT, 422 missing sha→recover, 401 stops + flags token, 403/429 sleeps to reset, network error backoff keeps unsynced, serial ordering, private events never leave, author name per user, pull merges partner files without touching own, own-device sha seeding.
makeEvent/validate, migrations per fixture version, ULID ordering, day/week keys across DST, base64 UTF-8 round trip (emoji notes), JSONL tolerant parse, mergeEvents.

Data linter: every step exercise exists; every rule id ∈ RULES; every requires string resolvable for BOTH users' declared inventories (pairs true/false, vest 10–40); each workout's estimate within 40–50 min at the lowest placement AND at mid-ladder; startFrom maps ordered and target existing steps; gates reference existing ladders/benchmarks; no duplicate ids; KB steps all gated behind swing-form-check; XP config has no per-step multiplier.
Event logs per schema version, two-user fixture histories, golden plan JSON, sample remote tree responses.

data_model:
All persisted user data is EVENTS; everything else is derived in memory.

EVENT ENVELOPE (every event)
{"v":1,"id":"01J6Z8Q3K7ABCDEF0123456789","ts":"2026-09-08T13:02:11.123Z","day":"2026-09-08","dev":"k3x9ab","user":"sean","type":"set.logged","private":false,"data":{...}}
- v: schema version; migrateEvent() upgrades old events at load.
- id: ULID-like (10-char base32 ms + 16 random chars); time-sortable, unique; dedupe key for merge.
- ts: UTC instant. day: LOCAL calendar day at the phone when it happened (streaks, weeks, scoreboard use day, never ts).
- dev: 6-char device id generated once per browser install. user: "sean" | "cat" (the profile that produced it; chosen at onboarding, switchable in Settings).
- private: true → never leaves the phone unless settings.syncMetrics is on (metric.logged defaults to true).

EVENT TYPES (data payload)
profile.updated  {"name":"Cat","programId":"warrior-v1","programStart":"2026-09-14","tz":"America/Chicago","restDow":0,
  "equipment":{"vestLb":[10,20,30,40],"dbLb":[8,10,12,20,35],"dbPairs":[8,10,12,20,35],"kbLb":[53],"treadmill":true}}   // partial merges; equipment is the shared set but recorded per user so each log is self-describing
assessment.recorded  (the 60-second placement quiz; one per user, re-takeable)
  {"pushup":{"style":"incline","reps":9},          // style ∈ wall|incline|knee|floor; reps = clean reps at that style
   "squatBw":18,                                    // bodyweight squats to a chair in 60 s
   "plankSec":30,
   "gobletTrial":12,                                // heaviest DB (8|10|12|20|35|0) for 10 comfortable goblet squats, 0 = bodyweight
   "pressTrial":8,                                  // heaviest DB (0|8|10|12|20) for 8 strict overhead presses
   "hinge":"new",                                   // new|some|confident
   "walkMph":3.4,                                   // comfortable brisk walk speed
   "vestLb":0}                                      // vest weight they can wear for 5 min walking
session.started  {"sessionId":"01J6...","workoutId":"A","phaseId":"foundation","weekIndex":0,"deload":false,"testDay":false,
  "plan":{ ...frozen Plan (see progression_engine)... }}   // frozen so "% of prescribed targets hit" is reproducible after any spec change
set.logged  {"sessionId":"01J6...","ladder":"pushup","stepId":"pushup.incline-low","exerciseId":"incline-pushup","setIndex":1,
  "reps":12,"seconds":null,"rounds":null,"perSide":false,
  "load":{"kind":"bw","lb":0},                     // kind ∈ bw|vest|db|kb|bw+vest|db+vest ; lb = external load ; n = 1|2 dumbbells
  "cardio":null,                                    // treadmill sets: {"mode":"steady","minutes":25,"mph":3.5,"incline":10} or {"mode":"interval","rounds":8,"workSec":60,"restSec":90,"mphWork":5.5,"mphRest":3.0,"incline":1}
  "rpe":7,"done":true,"tempo":"3-1-1"}
  Key = (sessionId, ladder|exerciseId, setIndex); the event with the greatest (ts,id) wins → editing is another set.logged, undo/delete is set.logged with done:false.
session.finished   {"sessionId":"01J6...","durationSec":2710,"sessionRpe":8,"note":"swings felt good"}
session.abandoned  {"sessionId":"01J6...","reason":"time"}      // partial XP, no streak credit
rest.taken         {}                                            // explicit rest day; counts as the allowed weekly rest
ladder.override    {"ladder":"pushup","stepId":"pushup.floor","reason":"too easy"}   // engine replays from this ts at the new step
benchmark.recorded {"benchmarkId":"pushup-max","value":15,"unit":"reps"}  // also form checks: {"benchmarkId":"swing-form-check","value":1,"unit":"pass","checklist":["hinge-not-squat","flat-back","float-to-chest","10-clean-deadstop-35"]}
metric.logged (private:true) {"weightLb":178.4,"waistIn":34.5,"chestIn":40,"note":""}

REMOTE FILE  log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl on branch `data` (e.g. log/cat/p7q2mz/2026-09.jsonl)
line 1: {"_hdr":1,"schema":1,"app":"warriorlog","user":"cat","dev":"p7q2mz","month":"2026-09"}
then one event per line sorted by (ts,id). ~150 B/event × ~600 events/month ≈ 90 KB, far under the 1 MB Contents GET limit. Only device <dev> ever writes files under log/<user>/<dev>/. Private events are excluded unless syncMetrics.

storage_and_sync.local: IndexedDB database `warriorlog` v1 (src/store.js, ~40-line promise wrapper) with stores: events (keyPath id; indexes ts, part = `${user}/${dev}/${month}`, synced), files (keyPath path → {sha, count, fetchedAt, etag}), meta (kv: treeEtag, schemaVersion, backoffUntil, lastError). dispatch() awaits the IDB put (<5 ms) BEFORE the UI marks a set done, so a tap is durable before the screen changes. On startup all events are read (a year ≈ 8k events per user, ~1.2 MB, <100 ms), migrated if v < SCHEMA_VERSION, reduced once. localStorage `warriorlog.settings` holds only dev, user, token, tokenExpires, syncMetrics, restTimerSec, sound, activeSessionId, lastPull. navigator.storage.persist() requested on first launch. If IDB is unavailable (private mode / blocked), store.js falls back to an in-memory array mirrored to a localStorage JSON snapshot with a visible warning. The unsynced queue is the synced=0 index, so store and queue can never disagree. Body metrics (metric.logged, private:true) live in the same store and are filtered at the sync boundary. Both users can exist on one phone (events carry user); Settings → Switch user changes settings.user only.
storage_and_sync.remote: Same public repo warriorlog/warriorlog.github.io, orphan branch `data` (created once at deploy; app can self-create it via POST /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs {ref:'refs/heads/data', sha:<main head>} if GET /git/ref/heads/data is 404). Layout: log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl — one file per user per device per month; the device <dev> is the SOLE writer of log/*/<dev>/*; every phone reads every file. Legacy Pages builds only fire on pushes to `main`, so log commits never rebuild the site, the laptop never rebases, and a code force-push cannot touch logs. Each commit is authored as the logging user (author:{name:'Sean'|'Cat', email:'<user>@warriorlog.github.io'}) and committed by the token owner (SJJ363), so github.com shows 'Cat authored, SJJ363 committed'. No derived files are ever written (no state.json, no totals). Optional log/<user>/<dev>/metrics-<yyyy-mm>.jsonl only when syncMetrics is on.
storage_and_sync.sync_algorithm:
Common request shape: base https://api.github.com; headers Authorization: Bearer <settings.token>, Accept: application/vnd.github+json, X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28, Content-Type: application/json on PUT/POST; 15 s AbortController timeout. All of sync runs single-flight under navigator.locks.request('warriorlog-sync', fn) (fallback: module mutex + BroadcastChannel) because Contents writes must be serial. C = WARRIORLOG_CONFIG; O=C.owner, R=C.repo, B=C.dataBranch.

PUSH (flush) — steps:
 1. Select events where synced=0 AND dev === settings.dev AND (private=false OR settings.syncMetrics). Group by part (user/dev/month) → path `log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl` (metrics go to `metrics-<yyyy-mm>.jsonl` under the same dir). Normally only this phone's own partitions. If nothing is pending, skip to PULL.
 2. For each path, sequentially: content = header line + ALL local events for that partition (not just unsynced — the device is the sole writer so local is the truth), one JSON per line sorted by (ts,id). Capture eventCount BEFORE encoding. Encode: TextEncoder → bytes → base64 (chunked loop; never btoa on raw UTF-16). Refuse (status 'file-too-big') if bytes > 900 KB — cannot happen at ~90 KB/month; test pins the guard.
 3. sha = files[path].sha (may be undefined for a never-pushed file).
 4. PUT /repos/{O}/{R}/contents/log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl with body {"message":"log: cat 2026-09 (+7 events)","content":"<base64>","branch":"data","sha":"<sha or omitted>","author":{"name":"Cat","email":"cat@warriorlog.github.io"}} (author = the profile name of event.user; committer omitted → token owner).
 5. 201 (created) or 200 (updated): files[path] = {sha: res.content.sha, count: eventCount, fetchedAt: now}; mark exactly the events serialized (by id) synced=1; emit status 'synced'.
 6. 409 Conflict (sha stale) or 422 whose message mentions sha (file exists, none sent — e.g. after storage was cleared): GET /repos/{O}/{R}/contents/{path}?ref=data (JSON form → sha + base64 content; strip embedded newlines, atob → Uint8Array → TextDecoder). Parse JSONL tolerantly, migrate, mergeEvents(remote, local) = union by id; insert remote-only events into IDB (only possible if a previous install with the same dev wrote them). Rebuild content, PUT again with the fresh sha. Max 3 attempts, then status 'conflict-parked'; retried on the next trigger.
 7. 404: diagnose — GET /repos/{O}/{R}: 404 → 'token cannot see repo'; 200 → GET /repos/{O}/{R}/git/ref/heads/data: 404 → offer one-tap 'Create data branch' = GET /repos/{O}/{R}/git/ref/heads/main → POST /repos/{O}/{R}/git/refs {"ref":"refs/heads/data","sha":"<main sha>"} then retry.
 8. 401 or 403 'Bad credentials'/'Resource not accessible by personal access token': settings.tokenState='invalid', stop the queue, red banner on Today linking to Settings; never auto-retry.
 9. 403/429 with x-ratelimit-remaining: 0 or retry-after: meta.backoffUntil = now + max(retry-after s, x-ratelimit-reset − now, 60 s); status 'rate-limited'.
 10. Network failure / 5xx / timeout: events stay synced=0; exponential backoff 2, 4, 8 … s capped at 5 min with 20 % jitter; reset on success or 'online'. A PUT whose response was lost (commit landed, client timed out) surfaces as a 409 next time and merges cleanly (ids dedupe).

PULL — steps:
 1. GET /repos/{O}/{R}/git/trees/data?recursive=1 with If-None-Match: <meta.treeEtag>. 304 → nothing changed (free against the limit). 200 → store new ETag; take every blob path matching ^log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>\.jsonl$ (skip metrics-* unless syncMetrics, skip README).
 2. For each path whose tree sha differs from files[path].sha: if the path belongs to THIS device (dev === settings.dev) and files[path].sha is known → skip (we are the writer); if it belongs to this device but sha is unknown (fresh install / cleared storage) → fetch and merge, seeding files[path].sha so the next push is an update. Otherwise (partner's phone, or own user's other device) → GET /repos/{O}/{R}/contents/{path}?ref=data with Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json (raw text, no base64 decode, valid to 100 MB).
 3. Parse JSONL tolerantly (skip and count bad lines), migrateEvent each, validate, insert events whose id is unknown with synced=1 (they came from remote), record files[path] = {sha, fetchedAt}.
 4. Recompute: reduce → evalLadders → gamify per user → duo; render; toast 'pulled N events from M files' when N>0; settings.lastPull = now.

TRIGGERS: pull on app start (online and lastPull older than 60 s), on visibilitychange→visible, on pull-to-refresh on Today/Duo, and after every successful push. Push on session.finished/abandoned (immediate), visibilitychange→hidden, 'online' event, every 5 min while unsynced>0, and Settings → Sync now. Per-set writes are local only.

TOKEN TEST (Settings → Save/Test): GET /repos/{O}/{R} → 200 and permissions.push===true; GET /repos/{O}/{R}/git/ref/heads/data → 200; show 'Connected as <login> · write · data branch OK · rate limit N left'.
storage_and_sync.conflict_resolution: Three layers. (1) Structural: a path is owned by exactly one (user, device) partition, so concurrent writers to one path are always the same logical device (second tab, or a reinstall carrying a stale sha) — Sean's and Cat's phones never PUT the same path, and neither do two devices of the same user. (2) Optimistic concurrency: every PUT carries the last known blob sha; 409/422 means our view is stale → GET, union by event id, PUT again with the returned sha, bounded to 3 attempts. (3) Semantic: events are immutable facts; an edit of a set is a newer set.logged for the same (sessionId, ladder, setIndex) and the reducer applies the greatest (ts,id); deletion is done:false, never a removal; therefore merges can neither resurrect nor lose changes, and nothing derived (XP, streak, scoreboard) is ever reconciled — it is recomputed. Web Locks serialize two tabs on one phone; BroadcastChannel makes the other tab re-read IDB. Clock skew only affects ordering of edits to the same set within seconds on the same phone; ids break ties deterministically.
storage_and_sync.token_handling:
CREATION (Sean does this on github.com; the app only receives the pasted string). Both tokens are created under SJJ363 with the ORG as resource owner — GitHub docs confirm fine-grained PATs can access organization-owned repositories, the org must allow fine-grained PATs (default: allowed), and 'fine-grained personal access tokens created by organization owners will not need approval' (Sean is the org owner, so no approval step). Steps, once per phone: github.com → profile photo → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens → Generate new token. Token name 'warriorlog-sean' (then 'warriorlog-cat'). Expiration: Custom → 366 days (the maximum; type the date into the app's Settings so it nags 14 days ahead). Resource owner: select 'warriorlog' (the org appears because Sean is a member; if it does not appear, the org has blocked fine-grained PATs — fix under the org's Settings → Third-party Access → Personal access tokens → Settings → 'Allow access via fine-grained personal access tokens'). Repository access: Only select repositories → warriorlog/warriorlog.github.io. Repository permissions: Contents → Read and write (Metadata → Read is auto-selected as mandatory). Nothing else. Generate → copy once. Paste into that phone: Warriorlog → Settings → GitHub sync → token field → Save (the app runs the token test). Hand Cat's token to her phone privately (AirDrop / paste directly on her phone while logged in), never via a public channel; Cat needs no GitHub account.

STORAGE ON THE PHONE: localStorage warriorlog.settings.token, plain string. WebCrypto with a co-located key is theatre; the honest threat model is 'any JS on this origin can read it'. Mitigations that actually matter: the site is its own origin (warriorlog.github.io) with zero third-party scripts, a CSP meta (default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com; img-src 'self' data:), all user text escaped through the html`` template, the token only ever sent as an Authorization header to api.github.com (never in a URL, never logged, never inside an event — sync refuses to push if any event string contains the token), masked in Settings (last 4), 'Forget token' button, and a fully functional sync-off mode.

BLAST RADIUS if a token leaks (Contents read/write on one public repo): CAN read/write/delete files and create commits on any branch of warriorlog.github.io (deface the site on main until reverted; delete logs on data — recoverable from git history and from the phones' local copies). CANNOT touch any other repo or the org's settings, change Pages settings (Administration), modify .github/workflows (separate Workflows permission), create issues/PRs, or act after expiry/revocation. Response: revoke that one token in Settings → Fine-grained tokens (the other phone keeps working), `git log` on both branches to revert foreign commits. GitHub secret scanning also flags github_pat_ strings pushed to public repos.
storage_and_sync.offline_queue: The queue is the synced=0 index on the events store — exactly as durable as the log and unable to drift. State machine in sync.js: idle → pushing → idle | backoff(n) | rate-limited(until) | needs-token | conflict-parked; any trigger re-enters from a non-pushing state; navigator.onLine is a hint only (a real fetch failure is the truth). A workout never blocks on sync: dispatch() returns after the IDB put and render. UI: a small dot in the bottom nav — grey synced, amber N pending (tap → Settings), red needs attention (auth/conflict). A phone offline for a week pushes one commit per touched month, not one per event. Background Sync (Chromium/Android) registers tag 'warriorlog-flush' on failure; iOS has none, so flush also runs on every foreground. The service worker never intercepts api.github.com, so there is no dependency on it for sync. Settings has Export JSON (all events incl. private) / Import as the disaster-recovery path for local-only body metrics.
storage_and_sync.rate_limits_and_size: Primary limit 5,000 requests/hour per PAT (each phone has its own PAT, so two independent budgets); secondary limits 80 content-creating requests/minute and 500/hour; 403/429 with retry-after / x-ratelimit-reset honoured; conditional GETs returning 304 cost nothing. Expected use per phone: ~2 PUTs per session (finish + hide) × 6/week ≈ 12 writes/week; pulls 1–3 GETs per open (tree usually 304). Even a pathological per-set flush stays under 1 % of limits. Sizes: ~150 B/event × ~600 events/month ≈ 90 KB per file (~120 KB base64 per PUT); the Contents GET 1 MB limit is never approached and pulls use the raw media type anyway; sync.js refuses files > 900 KB. Commits: ~600/year across both phones on the data branch, zero Pages builds. App shell ≈ 150 KB + data JSON ≈ 80 KB. Pulls are skipped when x-ratelimit-remaining < 50; never more than one in-flight request per phone.

- install: cache.addAll(SHELL.map(u => new Request(u, {cache:'reload'}))) then skipWaiting(). activate: delete caches ≠ CACHE, clients.claim().
- fetch: ignore non-GET, cross-origin (api.github.com), and any URL containing '/log/'. Same-origin shell URL → respond from cache immediately (instant launch, fully offline); if not cached → network then cache. Navigations fall back to cached './index.html'.
- revalidateShell(): triggered by a 'check-update' message from the page on load and on visibilitychange→visible (rate-limited to once per 5 min). Fetch every SHELL URL with {cache:'no-cache'} (forces conditional revalidation against Pages, which serves ETags). Only if ALL fetches succeed: compare each ETag (fallback: byte length + last-modified) with the cached response's; write all fresh responses into the cache; if any differed → clients.matchAll → postMessage({type:'update-ready'}). The page shows an 'Update ready — tap to reload' toast, deferred while a session is active (reload is safe anyway; every set is already in IDB). Registration: navigator.serviceWorker.register(CONFIG.basePath + 'sw.js', {scope: CONFIG.basePath, updateViaCache:'none'}). Guarantee: at most one stale launch per deploy, no version to forget, no CI. Residual staleness is the Pages CDN's own max-age=600.

Targets ≥56 px, 18 px+ text, touch-action:manipulation, user-select:none on controls, 100dvh + safe-area insets, no layout shift, prefers-reduced-motion honoured. base_path_handling: The app is path-agnostic by construction, with ONE config value for the deploy: config.js → window.WARRIORLOG_CONFIG.basePath = '/' (org site https://warriorlog.github.io/). Rules: (1) every href/src in index.html is relative (./style.css, ./src/app.js, ./manifest.webmanifest, ./icons/…); (2) every ES module import is relative and every data fetch is new URL('../data/program.json', import.meta.url) — never '/data/…'; (3) manifest start_url/scope/icons are relative and resolve against the manifest URL; (4) sw.js resolves its SHELL list with new URL(p, self.location) and is registered at CONFIG.basePath + 'sw.js' with scope CONFIG.basePath — this is the single place basePath is consumed (plus share links); (5) in-app navigation is a hash router (#/today, #/session/:id, #/duo, #/progress, #/history, #/body, #/settings, #/setup), so GitHub Pages never serves a deep path and no 404.html trick is needed; (6) the only absolute origin in code is https://api.github.com. To deploy at a sub-path (e.g. https://insurtechdaily.io/warriorlog/ as a project site) change basePath to '/warriorlog/' — and in practice even that only matters for SW scope, because everything else is relative. Verification: `python3 -m http.server 8098` inside the folder → http://localhost:8098/ (root case); the same server started from the parent folder → http://localhost:8098/warriorlog/ (sub-path case, with basePath temporarily '/warriorlog/'); both live in .claude/launch.json as configs 'root' and 'subpath'.

{workoutId:'A', phaseId:'foundation', weekIndex:0, deload:false, testDay:false, estMinutes:46,
 blocks:[{kind:'strength', items:[{ladder:'squat', stepId:'squat.goblet12', exerciseId:'goblet-squat', name:'Goblet squat', cues:[...], stopIf:'...', load:{kind:'db',lb:12,n:1},

RULES registry (closed; program.test.js and validate at load reject unknown ids). Each rule is (s, args, ctx) → boolean where s = one performance record for a ladder in one session {reps[], minReps, seconds[], rounds, rpeMax, allDone, cardioDone}:
 all_sets_reps_gte {reps, rpeMax?, consecutive}: every set done && every reps ≥ reps && (rpeMax==null || s.rpeMax ≤ (rpeMax ?? spec.rpeCap))
 min_reps_lt {reps, consecutive}: any set reps < reps  (regress)
 time_gte {seconds, rpeMax?, consecutive} / min_time_lt {seconds}  (holds, carries)
 rounds_gte {rounds, rpeMax?, consecutive}  (EMOM / intervals)
 total_reps_within {reps, minutes, consecutive}: session total reps ≥ reps and first→last set ≤ minutes  (density)
 cardio_done {rpeMax, consecutive}: steady cardio completed at ≥ minutes[0] with rpe ≤ rpeMax
 sessions_gte {n}: step performed n times (time-gated technique steps: hinge drill, dead-stop swings)
 benchmark_gte {id, value} / benchmark_lte: latest benchmark.recorded for id compared  (gates: swing-form-check)
 ladder_at_or_past {ladder, stepId}: ctx.ladders[ladder].stepIndex ≥ index of stepId  (cross-ladder gate)

prescribe(spec, U, today):
 1. weekIndex = floor((today − U.profile.programStart)/7d) in day keys. phase = last phase whose weeks contain weekIndex AND whose advanceWhen (e.g. sessions_gte 18) is satisfied — the calendar cannot outrun completed work.
 2. deload = (trainingWeek % spec.deload.everyNthWeek === everyNthWeek−1) OR fatigue (last 3 finished sessions each missed ≥ 2 targets, or mean sessionRpe over windowDays ≥ 8.5). Deload: sets × volumeScale (ceil, min 2), same loads, ladders frozen (perf records flagged deload are ignored by evalLadder). testDay = deload week AND a benchmark whose everyWeeks has elapsed is due AND the rotation lands on F → workoutId 'TEST' (records benchmark.recorded events; PR → XP).
 3. workoutId = template.rotation[U.counts.sessionsFinished % 6]; missed days shift, never skip. Today shows 'Rest day — tap to log' if today is restDow and nothing is logged (rest.taken keeps streaks). A 'Do a different workout' picker is offered but the default is the rotation.
 4. For each block item with a ladder: steps = resolveSteps(L, U.profile.equipment) — drop steps whose requires (bw | vest:<lb> | db:<lb> | db:<lb>:pair | kb:53 | treadmill) the inventory cannot satisfy, swap a pair-requiring step for its singleAlt when no pair exists, drop altOnly steps when the pair exists. pos = evalLadder(L, steps, U) (below). step = steps[pos.index]. sets = item.sets (× volumeScale if deload). Targets by double progression: reps target = clamp(lastMinRepsOnThisStep + 1, lo, hi) when the last session on this step had allDone, else lo; a freshly reached step starts at lo; holds/carries use seconds the same way; intervals/EMOM use rounds = clamp(lastRounds + 1, lo, hi); zone-2 uses minutes = clamp(last + 5, lo, hi) × item.scale. Load resolved by resolveLoad(step.load, equipment) per spec.loadRules (largest owned DB ≤ lb; vest nearest ≤ lb else declared tempo+2 reps substitution). Circuit blocks (E) use each ladder's current step − stepOffset (one step easier under fatigue) and the current vest weight from the pushup ladder's vest step if reached, else none. why/unlockHint strings come from the step's advance rule. If pos.gateBlocked, the item shows the gate (e.g. 'Pass the swing form check to earn the 53 lb bell') and the form-check card appears on Today.
 5. fitToTime: estimate = Σ warmup minutes + Σ over sets (reps × exercise.estSecPerRep + restSec) + conditioning minutes; if > sessionMinutes[1], shrink flex blocks (rounds −1, then minutes −5, then drop the last core set) until it fits; if < sessionMinutes[0], add one round/5 min to the flex block. program.test.js asserts every workout fits for both the lowest placement and mid-ladder fixtures.

evalLadder(L, steps, U) — replayed from history so a rule tweak or re-sync recomputes cleanly:
 index = startIndex from L.startFrom (assessment field → map lookup: largest key ≤ value, or exact style match; default 0); floor = index (regression never goes below the placement step). hits = misses = hold = 0.
 for s of U.perf[L.id] sorted by (day, ts):
   if an override with ts ≤ s.ts is newer than the last applied → index = its step, hits = misses = 0.
   if s.deload or s.stepId !== steps[index].id → continue   (deload work and circuit-day work never move a ladder)
   step = steps[index]
   hit = RULES[step.advance.rule](s, step.advance, ctx); miss = step.regress ? RULES[step.regress.rule](s, step.regress) : s.minReps < step.reps[0]
   if hit { hits++; misses = 0 } else if miss { misses++; hits = 0 } else { hits = 0; misses = 0 }
   if hold > 0 { hold--; continue }
   if hits ≥ step.advance.consecutive && index < steps.length−1:
       next = steps[index+1]; if gateOk(next.gate, ctx) { index++; hits = 0; stepsGained.push({day:s.day, from, to}) } else gateBlocked = next.gate   (at most spec.advanceCapPerSession = 1 per session)
   else if misses ≥ (step.regress?.consecutive ?? spec.regress.consecutive) && index > floor: { index--; misses = 0; hold = spec.regress.holdSessions }
 return {stepId, index, hitsInRow, missesInRow, holdSessions, lastMinReps, gateBlocked, unlockHint, stepsGained}
 gateOk(gate): every clause in gate.all passes (benchmark_gte swing-form-check for hinge.kb-deadstop; ladder_at_or_past for row.kb53) — the 53 lb bell is earned identically by both users.

gamify.js (per user, from gamification.json): session XP = Σ sets done × perSetDone + Σ sets hitting target × perSetTargetHit + allTargetsHit if targetsHit === targetsPrescribed + sessionFinish (or abandonedFinish) + ladderAdvance per stepsGained on that day + benchmarkPR + formCheckPass + perZone2Minute × zone-2 minutes + restDayLogged. No step/load multiplier (fairness). level = largest n with base·n(n+1)/2 ≤ xp; rank = ranks[floor((level−1)/5)] + roman sub-rank. Streak: walk day keys backward from today; a day counts if a finished session or rest.taken exists; a missing day is forgiven once per trailing 7 days (the rest day) and once more per trailing 30 (grace); otherwise the streak ends; best tracked. Badges: predicate registry (sessions_gte, ladder_reached, streak_gte, benchmark_gte/lte, sets_with_load_kind_gte, zone2_minutes_gte, xp_gte); earnedAt = ts of the first event after which the predicate is true (computed by replaying per session).

duo.js (pure, both users' derived states): partnerTrainedToday = partner has session.finished (or started) with day === today. duoStreak: a day is a duo day if BOTH have a finished session; a day where BOTH rested is forgiven once per 7; any other day breaks it. Weekly scoreboard: week = ISO Monday–Sunday in local day keys; per category compute each user's metric over that week — xp_gained (XP of sessions in week), targets_hit_pct (Σ targetsHit / Σ targetsPrescribed from frozen plans, ×100), ladder_steps_gained (count of stepsGained in week), zone2_minutes (steady cardio minutes), sessions_finished; leader per category gets a crown (tie → both); week leader = more crowns; lastWeek result kept for the 'Result' card. Never compares reps or weight. Bosses: window = weeks relative to min(both programStart); progress = metric summed over both users within the window (sets_done, ladder_reps {ladder}, zone2_minutes, sessions_finished, xp); status active/defeated/failed; defeated → rewardXpEach added to both users' XP (gamify reads duo results for boss XP in a second pass) and badge id granted to both. Duo badges: duo_streak_gte, both_ladder_reached, boss_defeated.

Fast-but-safe is encoded: one-variable steps; 1 step per session per ladder; consecutive-hit unlocks (a ladder appears 2–3×/week, so ~one step per 4–7 days); rpeCap 8 on hits; regress after 2 misses then hold 1; technique steps time-gated; KB steps gated by hinge position AND a recorded form check; deload every 4th week or on fatigue; new steps start at lo reps; conditioning capped at 12 rounds; benchmarks only on deload weeks.

key_decisions.choice: Append-only, schema-versioned event log with `user` on every event; all totals derived by pure functions (reduce → engine → gamify → duo)
key_decisions.alternatives: Mutable session/profile documents with cached XP/streak; hybrid with snapshots
key_decisions.why: Merges become set-union, rule tweaks recompute history, a bug fix is a re-derive, and the two-player scoreboard is computed identically on both phones from the same events.

key_decisions.choice: log/<user>/<dev>/<yyyy-mm>.jsonl on an orphan `data` branch; each phone writes only its own partitions and reads all others
key_decisions.alternatives: Logs on main next to code (Design 0); one shared events file; per-session files
key_decisions.why: Sole-writer paths make clobbering impossible for two phones and two users; legacy Pages builds fire only on main so log commits never rebuild the site, the laptop never rebases, and a code force-push cannot delete logs.

key_decisions.alternatives: Expression strings with an evaluator; rules hard-coded per exercise
key_decisions.why: Machine-checkable, unit-tested once, extended by 'add a case + a test'.

key_decisions.choice: One set.logged per tap; edits are newer set.logged (LWW by ts,id); delete is done:false; plan frozen into session.started
key_decisions.why: One tap = one durable write; history stays honest; '% targets hit' is reproducible after any spec change.

key_decisions.choice: ~35 files: 10 src modules (views split per screen), 3 data files, 8 test files, no CI, no build
key_decisions.alternatives: Design 1's ~45-file tree with core/engine/gamify/ui subtrees and two workflows; Design 0's ~20 files
key_decisions.why: Every screen has a home, every pure module is small enough for a future Claude Code session to load whole, and there is no pipeline to understand before shipping a change.

risks: 1. Org OAuth restrictions: new orgs block unapproved OAuth apps (GitHub CLI) by default; `gh repo create` fails with 403 until restrictions are removed or the CLI is approved (deploy step 2). 2. PAT visibility: if the org's PAT policy is ever switched to 'Restrict', the org disappears from the Resource owner list and existing tokens start failing (401/403 → red banner); the fix is the org setting, not the app. 3. Token expiry (max 366 days) silently stops sync on that phone — the app nags 14 days ahead when the expiry date is entered and shows a red banner on 401; workouts keep logging locally. 4. Public repo: both users' workout logs (names 'Sean'/'Cat', exercises, reps) are public; body metrics stay on-phone unless opted in; no locations or emails beyond the display addresses. 5. iOS storage eviction for a Safari tab unused 7 days: mitigated by home-screen install, storage.persist(), and the data branch as a full backup (Pull all rebuilds everything except local-only metrics — Export JSON covers those). 6. Stale shell for one launch after a deploy (Pages CDN max-age 600 + SWR): accepted; the toast covers it. 7. Two phones training simultaneously on one set of equipment: the app does not schedule equipment; the rotation makes both phones suggest the same workout letter on the same day only if their finished-session counts align — Today's 'Do a different workout' picker is the escape hatch. 8. Cat's token is created by Sean, so revocation and expiry are Sean's job; both tokens are listed in README with dates. 9. Program safety: rules encode RPE caps, one-step advances, regress/hold, deloads and the form-check gate, but no app sees form; exercise cues and stopIf notes are the guardrails and sharp pain is a stop. 10. Unconfirmed equipment (vest weights, dumbbell pairs) is asked at setup and every load resolves against it with declared substitutions; a wrong answer yields wrong loads until corrected in Settings. 11. Clock/timezone: day keys are stamped at event time; both users are assumed in the same timezone for the shared week; travel could shift a day at the edges. 12. Rate limits are far away, but a retry loop could hit the 500/h content-creating limit: single-flight, bounded retries and rate-limit sleeps prevent it. 13. Rule changes rewrite history (badges/XP/scoreboard can shift retroactively): accepted by design; frozen plans preserve what was prescribed. 14. Two tabs on one phone: Web Locks + BroadcastChannel; worst case a 409 merge. 15. If `data` is ever deleted or force-pushed from the laptop, phones still hold their own partitions and re-push them (409/422 → merge), but partner history would need the other phone to re-push — CLAUDE.md forbids touching the data branch from the laptop.
